clue.text: Violent emotion as parts of cardinal's office are swapped round

indicators.note: the two parts change places, so the second word is brought to the front

parts.note: a cardinal's office or dignity is the red hat, here taken as its two words

explanation.surface: A cardinal's household is in turmoil as departments trade places, stirring strong feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Are swapped round' moves HAT ahead of RED in REDHAT. A cardinal is made by receiving the red hat, so the phrase stands for the office.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense loathing is a powerful feeling, fairly called a violent emotion.

clue.text: Taking place simultaneously in the past

definitions.meaning: things done together happen at the same moment

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both 'together, at the same moment' and 'formerly, once'.

clue.text: Woolgathering clergyman goes over lake

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece sits above, or over, the second

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a clergyman
Erie is one of the Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A distracted priest drifts across a lake, lost in thought.
explanation.definitionFit: Woolgathering is idle daydreaming, a state of dreamy musing.

clue.text: Girl's dowry

definitions.meaning: A girl's name, short for Dorothy; the 's is 'is'
a dowry, from the French word

explanation.definitionFit: Dot is a pet name for Dorothy, and also an old word for a marriage portion.

clue.text: School supplied, with whisky (an unknown quantity) and mush

parts.note: malt is malt whisky
in algebra x, y and z stand for unknown quantities

explanation.surface: A school is stocked with whisky and some mysterious porridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Mush is sickly sentimentality, the same thing as cloying sentiment in art or song.

clue.text: Horse almost runs into' farm animal

indicators.note: the word is not quite complete, losing its final letter

parts.note: a steed is a horse
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A horse nearly bolts into another beast in the farmyard.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray apostrophe after 'into' is a printing mark and plays no part; 'runs into' reads as a collision but 'into' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A steer is a young castrated bull, a beast kept on farms for beef.

clue.text: Cheer loveless writer, an upper-class twit

parts.note: hooray is a cheer

indicators.note: love is zero in tennis, so the letter O is taken away

parts.note: O. Henry was an American short-story writer

explanation.surface: Applaud the author who has lost his romance, a foolish toff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loveless' removes O (love, a nil score in tennis) from OHENRY. The answer is a British term for a loud, braying, rich young man.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is British slang for a brash, wealthy young man from the upper classes.

clue.text: Bill and Joseph, having got on vessel, are put off

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: an ad, advertisement, is a bill or poster
Jo is short for Joseph
an urn is a vessel

explanation.surface: Two men board a ship and then find their plans postponed.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjourn a meeting is to postpone or defer it to a later time.

clue.text: I engaged in diplomacy without speaking

indicators.note: the letter is put to work inside the other word, as if employed there

parts.note: tact is diplomacy, delicacy in dealing with people

explanation.surface: A diplomat says they were busy with negotiation while staying silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tacit is understood or implied, unspoken rather than said aloud.

clue.text: Conquistador has not succeeded getting surgeon aboard vessel

indicators.note: the surgeon is placed on board, inside the other letters
the conquistador's name lacks the following letter

parts.note: Hernán Cortés was the Spanish conquistador who conquered Mexico
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees
a vet is a veterinary surgeon

explanation.surface: A Spanish adventurer fails, though a doctor joins him on his ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has not' removes S from CORTES, giving CORTE, and VET goes aboard it.
explanation.definitionFit: A corvette is a small warship, a kind of naval vessel.

clue.text: Thing to offer in opposition

explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word means an item; as a verb it means to raise a protest against.

clue.text: Force girl to follow soak back to dry land

indicators.note: the force and girl come after the reversed soak
the word is read backwards

parts.note: to ret flax is to soak it
the RAF is the Royal Air Force
Irma is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl is compelled to trail after a drunkard on the way home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' turns RET into TER. 'Soak' in the surface suggests a drunk, but here it means to steep in water.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase names solid ground as opposed to the sea, so firm dry land.

clue.text: Cassoulet is effervescent

definitions.meaning: a French stew packed with haricot beans

explanation.definitionFit: Literally a stew laden with pulses; figuratively an idiom for lively and energetic.

clue.text: To do nothing, enter any number

indicators.note: the number goes into the other letters

parts.note: ut is the old name for the note doh in sol-fa
N stands for any number in mathematics
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Asked to idle, a crowd of indeterminate size comes in.
explanation.walkthrough: UT is the older name of the first sol-fa note, now usually doh.
explanation.definitionFit: Unto is an archaic preposition meaning towards or as far as, the same sense as plain to.

clue.text: Fish dive in this position

definitions.meaning: a diving posture with legs straight and body bent at the hips

explanation.definitionFit: It is both a toothy freshwater fish and the jackknife-like body posture used in diving.

clue.text: A gun gilly had initially broken, having no serious intent

indicators.note: broken signals the letters are smashed up and reassembled
only the first letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: A gamekeeper's assistant had his gun fail, and everyone treated it as a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken' rearranges A, GUN, GILLY and H (first letter of 'had', signalled by 'initially'). A gilly is a Scottish hunting or fishing attendant.
explanation.definitionFit: Done in jest or mockingly, rather than in earnest.

clue.text: Employ some of 26

indicators.note: only a part of the answer to clue 26 is taken

parts.note: refers to the solution of clue 26

explanation.surface: Make use of part of another answer in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: To employ a tool is to make use of it, a straight synonym.

clue.text: This answer is male, and is promiscuous

definitions.text: This answer is male, and is promiscuous

indicators.note: promiscuous means mixed up and indiscriminate, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: The solution describes a man who sleeps around.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of 'is male, and' are mixed up, signalled by 'promiscuous', and the whole clue describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A womaniser is a man who pursues many women, fitting a promiscuous male.

clue.text: Hurry up and vote on game being played

indicators.note: a game being played is in motion, so its letters are moved around with the others

explanation.surface: An urgent call to cast your vote on the match in progress.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom urges someone to hasten, the same as telling them to be quick.

clue.text: Acquit a misbehaving marine

indicators.note: the letters behave badly, ending up out of order

explanation.surface: A court clears a badly behaved soldier of the Royal Marines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marine' looks like a noun, a soldier; it is the adjective meaning of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Marine and aquatic both describe things living in or relating to water.

clue.text: Fell, having reportedly gone rather quickly

indicators.note: reportedly signals a word that sounds like another

parts.note: hied means hastened, went quickly

explanation.surface: Someone fell, having apparently moved too fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fell' looks like the past of fall; it is the noun for an animal's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A fell is an animal's skin or pelt, which is what a hide is.

clue.text: Journalist observed cutter

parts.note: a hack is a journalist, often a disparaging term
saw means observed

explanation.surface: A reporter noticed someone with a knife.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacksaw is a fine-toothed saw for metal, a cutting tool.

clue.text: Place that's covered in lutetium

indicators.note: the abbreviation sits inside the symbol, which covers it

parts.note: Lu is the chemical symbol for lutetium
i.e. is short for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A location coated with a rare earth metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lieu means place, as in the phrase in lieu of, meaning in place of.

clue.text: In the city, I put up people

indicators.note: in a down entry the whole sequence is written upwards

parts.note: taken as written
EC is the postcode area for the City of London
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone describes erecting a building for residents in town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up' turns the whole run INECI into ICENI. The Iceni were an ancient British tribe led by Boudicca.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iceni were a tribe of ancient Britain, so a people.

clue.text: Complained as boat's timekeeper went on cruise, wasting time

parts.note: a ship's bell marks the watches on board

indicators.note: the word wastes away, losing the letter for time

parts.note: yachted means sailed for pleasure

explanation.surface: A ship's officer grumbled during a pleasure cruise that time was lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wasting' removes T from YACHTED, leaving YACHED.
explanation.definitionFit: Bellyached is slang for grumbled, moaned or complained.

clue.text: I twice interrupted chap wanting to stay abed

indicators.note: the letters break into the name at two separate places
twice says the single letter goes into the name a second time, at another spot

parts.note: Len is a man's name

explanation.surface: Someone keeps cutting in on a man who just wants to stay in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twice' means the one I goes into LEN two times, separately: LEN becomes LIEN, then LIEIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie in is to stay in bed late in the morning.

clue.text: Position given to a girl

parts.note: a berth is a position, a job or place

explanation.surface: A job is offered to a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Bertha is a female first name, so an example of a girl, the usual crossword way of defining given names.

clue.text: Dance said to attract attention

definitions.meaning: a dance in which partners can be cut in on
a polite phrase to get someone's notice

explanation.definitionFit: It is a ballroom dance where one may cut in, and a polite phrase used to get notice.

clue.text: Swan 'or loaf

explanation.definitionFit: A male swan has this name, as does a rounded loaf of bread.

clue.text: Bishop once said this should be translated

indicators.note: to translate is to change into another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bishop once declared that this text needs translating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bishop' is a noun, but the answer is adjective-as-noun: a diocesan is the bishop of a diocese.
explanation.definitionFit: A diocesan is the bishop in charge of a diocese.

clue.text: Acknowledging applause for musical technique

definitions.meaning: taking a bow in thanks for clapping
the way a string player uses the bow

explanation.definitionFit: Bending in thanks to an audience, and also the way a violinist draws the bow.
